proof:
Source: steps (c1)–(c3) of the parent proof. This is the coordinate expression of d on ℝ × ℝ^N, i.e. Simon 6.2.17–2.21 (∂([[0,1]] × T) = {1} × T − {0} × T − [[0,1]] × ∂T) at the level of forms. Fix N, k, the differentiable β, and t, x, v.
1. Coordinates. By sibling coords (Submission.cmcdt_lpo_slice_coords N), choose a continuous linear equivalence L : ℝ × ℝ^N ≃L[ℝ] ℝ^{N+1} with L(s, y) = WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons s (WithLp.ofLp y)) for all s, y, and L(1, 0) = EuclideanSpace.single 0 1. Rewrite the goal right-to-left with these two identities (simp only [← hL, ← hL1]). Then every ι(s, y) becomes L(s, y), in particular Jv_i = L(0, v_i), and e₀ becomes L(1, 0).
2. Derivatives of evaluations. Fix a tuple u : Fin (k+1) → ℝ^{N+1} and a point y. The map y ↦ β(y)(u) is β followed by the continuous linear map ContinuousAlternatingMap.apply ℝ (Euclid (N+1)) ℝ u. Since β is differentiable at y, the chain rule gives derivative (apply u) ∘ Dβ(y) at y, so fderiv ℝ (y ↦ β y u) y = (apply u) ∘ Dβ(y).
3. Derivatives of the coordinate paths.
 - s ↦ (s, x) has derivative (1, 0) ((hasDerivAt_id s).prodMk (hasDerivAt_const s x)). Since L is continuous linear, s ↦ L(s, x) has derivative L(1, 0) at every s (HasFDerivAt.comp_hasDerivAt).
 - x' ↦ (t, x') has derivative ι₂ := ContinuousLinearMap.inr ℝ ℝ (Euclid N). So x' ↦ L(t, x') has derivative L ∘ ι₂ at every x', and (L ∘ ι₂)(y) = L(0, y).
4. Expansion. Put w := (i ↦ L(0, v_i)) : Fin (k+1) → ℝ^{N+1} and W := Fin.cons L(1, 0) w : Fin (k+2) → ℝ^{N+1}. By exteriorDerivative_apply (β is differentiable at L(t, x)):
 dβ(L(t, x))(W) = Σ_{i : Fin (k+2)} (−1)^i • D[y ↦ β(y)(i.removeNth W)](L(t, x))(W i).
 Split off the index 0 with Fin.sum_univ_succ, and write the right-hand side of the claim as A + (−S) (sub_eq_add_neg). It remains to identify the i = 0 term with A = deriv φ t, where φ(s) := β(L(s, x))(w), and the sum over i = j.succ with −S.
5. The term i = 0. Here (−1)^0 • z = z, removeNth 0 W = Fin.tail W = w (Fin.removeNth_zero, Fin.tail_cons), and W 0 = L(1, 0) (Fin.cons_zero). By steps 2 and 3 and the chain rule, φ has derivative ((apply w) ∘ Dβ(L(t, x)))(L(1, 0)) at t. So deriv φ t equals this value, which by step 2 is D[y ↦ β(y)(w)](L(t, x))(L(1, 0)), the i = 0 term.
6. The terms i = j.succ, for j : Fin (k+1).
 (a) W (j.succ) = w j = L(0, v_j) (Fin.cons_succ).
 (b) j.succ.removeNth W = U_j := Fin.cons L(1, 0) (i ↦ L(0, (Fin.removeNth j v) i)). Recall Fin.removeNth p f = f ∘ p.succAbove, and compare entries with Fin.cases. At index 0: j.succ.succAbove 0 = 0, so both sides are L(1, 0). At index l.succ: j.succ.succAbove l.succ = (j.succAbove l).succ (Fin.succ_succAbove_succ), so the left side is w (j.succAbove l) = L(0, v (j.succAbove l)), which equals the right side L(0, (removeNth j v) l).
 (c) By steps 2 and 3 and the chain rule, x' ↦ β(L(t, x'))(U_j) has derivative ((apply U_j) ∘ Dβ(L(t, x))) ∘ (L ∘ ι₂) at x. Hence D[x' ↦ β(L(t, x'))(U_j)](x)(v_j) = ((apply U_j) ∘ Dβ(L(t, x)))(L(0, v_j)) = D[y ↦ β(y)(U_j)](L(t, x))(W (j.succ)).
 (d) (−1)^{j.succ} = (−1)^{j+1} = −(−1)^j (Fin.val_succ, pow_succ, mul_neg_one, neg_smul).
 So the j.succ term equals −((−1)^j • D[x' ↦ β(L(t, x'))(U_j)](x)(v_j)). Summing over j and using Finset.sum_neg_distrib, these terms add up to −S.
7. Steps 4–6 give the stated identity. □
key_steps: Rewrite ι(s, y) = L(s, y) and e₀ = L(1, 0) with sibling coords.
y ↦ β(y)(u) has derivative (apply u) ∘ Dβ(y); s ↦ L(s, x) has derivative L(1, 0); x' ↦ L(t, x') has derivative L ∘ inr.
Expand dβ by exteriorDerivative_apply and split off i = 0 (Fin.sum_univ_succ, sub_eq_add_neg).
i = 0: removeNth 0 W = tail W = Jv and W 0 = e₀, so the chain rule identifies the term with deriv φ t.
i = j.succ: W j.succ = Jv_j and j.succ.removeNth W = Fin.cons e₀ (J ∘ removeNth j v) (Fin.cases, Fin.succ_succAbove_succ); the chain rule along x' ↦ L(t, x') and (−1)^{j+1} = −(−1)^j give −S.
